messages.content: I want one clean comparison before we choose. Put the Westin, Holiday Inn Resort, and Seafarer side by side for August 22 through 28. Use the complete six-night cost, not just the room quote, and tell me exactly how we would get from each hotel to the beach.

I’ll compare the same stay for two adults and one king room, then separate room price, mandatory charges, parking, and estimated taxes. I’ll also verify whether beach access is on the property or requires crossing a road. Do you want refundable rates only, or should I include a cheaper nonrefundable rate if one appears?
Refundable only. We are not booking today, and I do not want a low number that depends on prepaying.

Understood. The three refundable room options I found are: Westin partial ocean-view king at $249 per night; Seafarer one-bedroom king suite at $219 per night; and Holiday Inn Resort king leisure room at $189 per night. I’m checking the fee and cancellation details before treating those as comparable.
The Westin quote says partial view. Please make sure that does not mean we are in a separate building away from the beach.

It does not. The partial ocean-view king is in the main Westin building. The hotel fronts the beach, and guests leave through the ocean-side grounds onto the hotel’s boardwalk over the dunes. No public street crossing is involved. The partial-view label describes the room’s sightline, not its location within a remote building.
Good. What is the actual Westin total?

For six nights, the Westin calculation is $1,494 room charge, $180 destination fee, $90 self-parking, and $301.68 in estimated lodging taxes and tax on mandatory charges. The comparable total is $2,065.68. The rate includes a partial ocean-view king and may be canceled without penalty through 11:59 p.m. local time on August 18. After that, the penalty is one night plus tax.
That matches the earlier figure. Now explain the Seafarer route without calling it beachfront if it really is across the road.

The Seafarer is not directly on the sand. From the hotel’s beach-side exit, you walk to North Beachview Drive, cross the two-lane road at the marked crossing, and continue along the public beach-access path over the dunes. The route is about 450 feet from the edge of the property to the sand, generally a two- to four-minute walk. There is no shuttle or drive involved, but there is a street crossing.
And the suite is meaningfully larger than the other rooms? My wife and I do not need a second bedroom, but a sitting area for six nights could be useful.

Yes. The quoted Seafarer option is a one-bedroom king suite with a separate sitting room and kitchenette, rather than a standard king guest room. It is the largest of these three room options. The listing does not promise an ocean view or balcony, so the extra space should not be read as a view upgrade.
Calculate that one all the way through, including anything due at the hotel.

The Seafarer total is $1,314 for six nights plus $157.68 in estimated lodging tax, for $1,471.68. Self-parking is included, and I found no mandatory resort or destination fee on this rate. The refundable deadline is 4:00 p.m. local time on August 20; a later cancellation is charged one night plus tax. That makes it $594 less than the Westin.
Now Holiday Inn. Its $189 rate looked cheapest, but I remember extra charges in the earlier total.

Correct. The base room amount is $1,134, but the property adds a $35 nightly resort charge, or $210 for the stay, plus $12 per night for self-parking, or $72. Estimated taxes and tax on the mandatory resort charge are $223.68. The complete six-night total is therefore $1,639.68.
Is its beach access actually direct? I do not want the hotel driveway described as beach access.

It is direct. From the ocean-facing side of the Holiday Inn, you cross the hotel’s lawn and use its dune boardwalk to the beach. You do not cross Beachview Drive or another public road. Depending on the room’s building location, there may be a walk through the resort grounds, but the route remains entirely on hotel property until the boardwalk reaches the sand.
What room and cancellation language should I carry forward for that one?

The comparable Holiday Inn rate is for a king leisure room. It does not guarantee an ocean view, balcony, or particular building. Cancellation is free through 6:00 p.m. local time on August 17; after that, the listed penalty is the first night plus tax. The $35 nightly resort charge and $12 nightly parking should stay in the notes because neither is reflected in the $189 headline rate.
Put all three in cost order, then tell me what we are actually paying extra for with each step up.

Seafarer is lowest at $1,471.68, with the largest room, included parking, and the latest cancellation deadline, but it requires crossing North Beachview Drive and has no guaranteed view. Holiday Inn is next at $1,639.68, which is $168 more; that premium buys direct, no-road-crossing beach access, while the room is a standard king with no guaranteed view. Westin is $2,065.68, another $426 above Holiday Inn and $594 above Seafarer; its advantages are the partial ocean view, direct beach boardwalk, and location beside Beach Village for walking to restaurants. Its cancellation deadline falls between the other two.
So the Westin is not buying us a full ocean view, and Holiday Inn’s headline savings are partly erased by $282 in resort and parking charges before tax. Is that a fair reading?

Yes. The Westin room guarantees only a partial ocean view, not an unobstructed one. At Holiday Inn, the resort charge and parking add $282 before related tax, taking the $1,134 room subtotal to the $1,639.68 complete estimate. Even after those additions, Holiday Inn remains $426 below the Westin.
Give me the decision version. Keep all three alive, but identify the exact room, total, beach route, and cancellation cutoff. Nothing should be booked.

Decision comparison for August 22-28, six nights for two adults; nothing has been booked. Seafarer Inn & Suites: one-bedroom king suite with separate sitting room and kitchenette, $1,471.68 including estimated taxes, parking included, and no mandatory resort fee found. Beach access requires crossing two-lane North Beachview Drive at the marked crossing and following the public dune path, about two to four minutes to the sand. Free cancellation ends at 4:00 p.m. local time on August 20. Holiday Inn Resort Jekyll Island: king leisure room with no guaranteed view or balcony, $1,639.68 including the $210 resort charge, $72 self-parking, and estimated taxes. Its lawn and dune boardwalk lead directly to the beach without crossing a public road. Free cancellation ends at 6:00 p.m. local time on August 17. The Westin Jekyll Island Beach Resort: partial ocean-view king in the main building, $2,065.68 including the destination charge, self-parking, and estimated taxes. Its ocean-side boardwalk provides direct beach access with no street crossing, and Beach Village dining is adjacent. Free cancellation ends at 11:59 p.m. local time on August 18. Seafarer is the value-and-space choice, Holiday Inn is the lower-cost direct-access choice, and Westin carries the highest price for the partial view and more walkable dining location.
